name: Airbus A220
summary: Clean-sheet 100–150-seat narrowbody designed by Bombardier and taken over by Airbus; flown in the US by Delta, JetBlue and Breeze.

wings: Low-mounted swept wing with plain tips — no winglets or sharklets
Long, slender high-aspect-ratio wing for the aircraft's size
engines: Two underwing geared turbofans whose nacelles look oversized for the slim body
Nacelles hang well ahead of the wing leading edge, close to the ground
fuselage: Slim 5-abreast fuselage, noticeably narrower than a 6-abreast single-aisle
Rounded nose with a four-pane windshield and a short, stubby profile
tail: Tall swept fin with a nearly straight leading edge
Tapered tailcone ending in a small APU exhaust

tellTales: Huge round engines on a slender narrow body
Clean wingtips with no winglets on a modern-looking twinjet
Big square cabin windows on a 5-abreast tube

confusedWith.howToTell: The A220 has much bigger engines, plain wingtips and a wider 5-abreast body; the E175 has small engines, canted winglets and a 4-abreast double-bubble body.
The A220 is slimmer and shorter with plain wingtips and proportionally huge engines; the A320 has wingtip fences or sharklets and a wider 6-abreast fuselage.
Both carry big geared-fan engines, but the A220 has plain wingtips, a narrower body and larger square windows; the A320neo always has tall sharklets.

usCount.source: Airline fleet data (Delta ~80, JetBlue ~50, Breeze ~50; planespotters.net)
